newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks stagnate, no changes foreseen.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks stagnate, no changes foreseen.

text.p: Croatian stocks were steady to lower in shrinking pre-Easter trade on Thursday and traders foresaw no major boosts on the market until mid-April.
"This downward period will continue for some time and trading is not likely to seriously pick up before the middle of April," said Igor Kos of Taurus brokerage.
Thursday's turnover shrank to 1.9 million kuna from almost 5 million on Wednesday and volume halved to 3,724 units.

Kos ascribed the lull in trading to the approaching Easter holidays and to investors holding back while waiting for the publication of business results of bluechips Zagrebacka Banka and drugs firm Pliva, due next month.
"All the stocks are still looking up to Zagrebacka and reflecting its trends. Market participants are looking for a new hot stock but haven't found it yet," he said.
Of 11 issues active on Thursday five fell, three were flat and three rose.
Zagrebacka was among the gainers, inching up 0.1 kuna to 1,850.1 on modest volume of 158 shares. Pliva traded flat at 450 kuna, selling 524 shares.
Pliva is fully listed at London Stock exchange and Zagrebacka's GDRs trade on Seaq international.
Zagrebacka's E-series preference stock was also among gainers, rising 20 kuna to 1,000 with 241 shares sold.
Investors were partly put off because of speculations about possible effects the voucher privatisation scheme may have on their investments, Kos said.
The authorities recently published a list of assets in over 800 companies to be distributed in exchange for vouchers to refugees and war victims, who, investors fear, may sell them off for pittances.
Kos singled out food processor Podravka and hotelier Laguna Porec as stocks which trade well and are relatively unaffected by price changes of the blue chips.
Podravka was Thursday's most actively traded stock and held its ground at 295 kuna on volume of 1,567 shares.
Laguna lost 2 kuna to 1,443, selling 323 units.
Another hotelier, Suncani Hvar, was the biggest decliner, losing 3 kuna to 60 on volume of 115 shares.
Chocolate maker Kras, long expected to become the next best-selling issue, lost seven kuna to 430, selling only 15 units.
"Kras is still a speculative issue. It fluctuates and hesitates, but maybe it still becomes a good stock," Kos said.
